radius.$description:
Two slots, because the mock only ever uses two true corner radii. Buttons are absent on purpose: every button in the mock is a pill (its radius is exactly half its height), so buttons carry `rounded-full` rather than a value from this scale — a fixed token would be wrong at any height but the one it was measured at.

Conversion: the mock is a 1440 CSS px wide design, so a 600 DPI render is 12000 px wide and the divisor is 12000 / 1440 = 8.3333 px per CSS px. An earlier revision of this file used 600 / 96 = 6.25, which over-reads every measurement by 1.3333x; that is what put `md` at 24px and `lg` at 28px. Re-derived 2026-08-29 against PDF page 1 (controls) and page 4 (surfaces), each calibrated independently: page 1's Button Primary (L) measures 400px tall at 600 DPI against a 48px design height, and page 4's task card measures 2332px wide against a 280px design width — both give 8.3333.

sm.$description: Control corner radius — text field, dropdown trigger, subtask checkbox. Measured from PDF page 1 'Text Field (Idle)': 27px at 600 DPI = 3.24 CSS px, rounded to 4px. Unchanged by the 2026-08-29 re-derivation: the old 6.25 divisor gave 4.32px, which rounded to the same 4px by coincidence.

md.$description: Surface corner radius — task cards, columns, modals, toasts, dropdown and menu popups, and every other panel on `bg-surface`. Measured from PDF page 4's task card: a 61.5px corner arc at 600 DPI = 7.4 CSS px, rounded to 8px. Was 24px, which was the Button Secondary pill read through the wrong divisor; no surface in the mock is anywhere near that round.
